It assumes data arises from an unknown distribution and models approximate this through parameterized functions. This leads to a dual structure: one of empirical observation (D) and theoretical prediction (M). The framework's failure mode occurs when N < complexity of M, causing overfitting. The 'Data Collection Scale Inflation' primitive introduces a scaling law where S grows exponentially with time, leading to high-dimensional spaces where traditional methods fail. This necessitates kernel-based methods in GSE for latent space discovery. The 'ISLR-ISLP Equivalence' primitive ensures that algorithmic content is preserved across platforms, enabling portable inference engines in GSI. Each primitive forms a closed-loop system where observables feed back into model refinement.
